deviceD: Notifications show while the app is open. When it is closed, the server sends alerts to the places below.
appD: The app shows your alerts as phone notifications, also when it is closed.
appHow: The app asks your server for new alerts about every 15 minutes. It needs the phone to allow notifications.
appBlocked: Notifications are blocked for this app. Allow them in the phone's settings.
appServer: Your server does not support this yet. Update the server to the latest version.
appFail: Could not turn it on. Try again.
appSent: Sent. It arrives in a moment.
deniedHelp: Notifications are blocked for this app. Allow them in your browser's or computer's settings.
localHow: Alerts pop up while the app is open. When it is closed, the places below can still reach you.
pushSwitch: Alerts when the app is closed
pushD: Alerts reach this device even when the app is closed. Open the app over https (for example your Tailscale address). On a phone, add it to the home screen first.
noSupport: This browser does not support push.
needHttps: Push needs https. Open the app over your https address.
ntfyD: A free notification service you can run on your own server.
ntfyLabel: ntfy topic URL (your own server, optional)
note: Telegram and webhooks send the alert text, including account names and amounts, over the internet to that service. Turn them on only if you are comfortable with that. WhatsApp has no free official way to message yourself. A Telegram bot or a webhook (Discord, Slack, Home Assistant, n8n) does the same job.
tgChat: Chat id (message your bot, then open api.telegram.org/bot…/getUpdates)
whD: Alerts sent to Discord, Slack, Home Assistant, n8n and similar.
whLabel: Webhook address (Discord, Slack, Home Assistant, n8n…)

t.needHttps: Push needs https and a browser that supports it
t.notReady: The app is not ready yet, try again
t.noDevice: No device is turned on yet
